# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH GRAM-POSITIVE BACILLI/COCCOBACILLI SUGGESTING LISTERI

# MONOCYTOGENES

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible after obtaining blood cultures and performing a lumbar puncture to obtain cerebrospinal fluid. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Acute meningitis
- Sanford keyword: Meningitis, bacterial, positive gram stain
- Tunkel et al., Clin Infect Dis, 2004, 39.1267-84
- Up-to-Date Article: Clinical features and diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis in adults
- Up-to-Date Article: Treatment of bacterial meningitis caused by specific pathogens in adults
- Van de Beek et al., Clin Microbiol Infect, 2016, 22.S37-S62
Therapy:
Preferred:

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q6h ($$$) R,DI
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU BAC MENING GRM POS BACILLI L. MONOCYTO
